items.followUp: Write the melting point and boiling point of potassium metal.

rubric.why: The melting point is one of the two required physical constants.
rubric.how: Award for 97.8 °C (or the commonly rounded value 98 °C).

rubric.why: The boiling point is the second required physical constant.
rubric.how: Award for 883 °C.

modelAnswer: Melting point of sodium = 97.8 °C (approximately 98 °C).
Boiling point of sodium = 883 °C.

items.followUp: Compare Rutherford’s and Bohr’s models of the atom, stating how electrons are arranged and when they exchange energy.

rubric.why: Both atomic models include a positively charged nucleus; identifying it gives a basic point of comparison.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the atom has a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.

rubric.why: Rutherford proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award for stating that electrons revolve around the nucleus in Rutherford’s model.

rubric.why: Bohr’s key improvement was that electrons occupy specific allowed orbits or energy levels.
rubric.how: Award for stating that electrons can occupy only fixed energy levels or stationary orbits.

rubric.why: Electrons in Bohr’s allowed stationary orbits do not continuously lose energy.
rubric.description: States the energy behaviour within a Bohr orbit
rubric.how: Award for stating that electrons do not radiate energy while remaining in an allowed orbit.

rubric.why: In Bohr’s model, electrons exchange energy when they move between allowed energy levels.
rubric.description: Explains energy exchange between Bohr orbits
rubric.how: Award for stating that an electron absorbs or emits energy when it jumps between orbits.

modelAnswer: Rutherford proposed that an atom has a small, dense, positively charged nucleus, with electrons revolving around it.
Rutherford’s theory did not assign electrons fixed energy levels.
Bohr proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus in specific fixed orbits, each with a definite energy.
Electrons in these stationary orbits do not radiate energy.
An electron absorbs or emits energy when it jumps from one orbit to another.

items.followUp: Define chemistry and briefly describe physical chemistry and biochemistry.

rubric.why: These are the central subjects included in the definition of chemistry.
rubric.how: Award for defining chemistry as the study of the composition, structure and properties of matter and the changes it undergoes.

rubric.why: Organic chemistry concerns carbon compounds, commonly described in the textbook as hydrocarbons and their derivatives.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is the study of hydrocarbons and their derivatives or organic compounds.

rubric.why: Inorganic chemistry covers elements and their compounds other than organic compounds.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is the study of elements and their compounds, excluding organic compounds.

rubric.why: These are common carbon-containing exceptions treated as inorganic compounds in the textbook classification.
rubric.how: Award for naming at least one appropriate exception, such as carbonates, bicarbonates, carbides or oxides of carbon.

modelAnswer: Chemistry is the branch of science that deals with the composition, structure and properties of matter and the changes it undergoes.
Organic chemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with hydrocarbons and their derivatives.
Inorganic chemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with all elements and their compounds except organic compounds.
Carbonates, bicarbonates, carbides and oxides of carbon are generally treated as inorganic compounds.

items.followUp: Explain the formation of an ionic bond between magnesium and oxygen atoms, including the ions formed.

rubric.why: An ionic bond forms through electron transfer and the attraction between the resulting oppositely charged ions.
rubric.how: Award for defining an ionic bond as the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions, formed by electron transfer.

rubric.why: A sodium atom has one electron in its outer shell and loses it during bond formation.
rubric.how: Award for stating that sodium, with electron arrangement 2,8,1, loses one electron.

rubric.why: Loss of one electron forms a positively charged sodium ion with a stable outer shell.
rubric.how: Award for giving Na⁺, preferably with the resulting arrangement 2,8.

rubric.why: A chlorine atom gains the electron transferred from sodium.
rubric.how: Award for stating that chlorine, with electron arrangement 2,8,7, gains one electron.

rubric.why: The resulting Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions attract and form sodium chloride.
rubric.how: Award for identifying Cl⁻ and the electrostatic attraction between Na⁺ and Cl⁻ that forms NaCl.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by the transfer of electrons.
A sodium atom has the electron arrangement 2,8,1 and loses its outermost electron: Na → Na⁺ + e⁻.
The sodium ion has the electron arrangement 2,8.
A chlorine atom has the electron arrangement 2,8,7 and gains the electron: Cl + e⁻ → Cl⁻.
The oppositely charged Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions attract each other and form an ionic bond in sodium chloride, NaCl.

items.followUp: Define evaporation and explain how wind speed and humidity affect its rate.

rubric.why: A complete definition identifies the change of state, its location at the liquid’s surface and that it can occur below the boiling point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a liquid changes into vapour from its surface, and 1 mark for stating that this occurs below the boiling point (or at temperatures below boiling).

rubric.why: More exposed liquid surface allows more particles to escape per unit time.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of surface area
rubric.how: Award for stating that increasing surface area increases the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: Higher temperature gives surface particles more kinetic energy, so more can escape into vapour.
rubric.how: Award for stating that increasing temperature increases the rate of evaporation, preferably with the kinetic-energy explanation.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface at a temperature below its boiling point.
A larger surface area increases the rate of evaporation because more liquid particles are exposed at the surface.
Increasing the temperature increases the kinetic energy of liquid particles.
More particles can then escape from the surface, so evaporation becomes faster.

rubric.why: Industrial chemistry concerns the industrial manufacture of chemical substances and the processes used for it.
rubric.how: Award for describing it as the study of methods or processes used to manufacture chemical substances on an industrial scale.

rubric.why: Analytical chemistry identifies what substances contain and may determine their amounts.
rubric.how: Award for describing it as the identification of components and/or determination of the composition of substances.

modelAnswer: Industrial chemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with methods and processes used to manufacture chemical substances on an industrial scale.
Analytical chemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with identifying the components of substances and determining their composition.

items.followUp: Name the three isotopes of hydrogen.

rubric.why: Protium is one of the isotopes of hydrogen.
rubric.how: Award for naming any one of protium, deuterium or tritium.

rubric.why: A second distinct hydrogen isotope is required.
rubric.description: Names a second, different hydrogen isotope
rubric.how: Award for naming another of protium, deuterium or tritium; do not award twice for the same isotope.

modelAnswer: Two isotopes of hydrogen are protium and deuterium.
(Tritium is the third isotope of hydrogen.)

items.followUp: What is the half-life of carbon-14, and how is it used to estimate the age of an ancient organic sample?

rubric.why: Carbon dating uses the radioactive isotope carbon-14.
rubric.how: Award for stating that carbon dating uses carbon-14 to determine age.

rubric.why: The age is estimated from the carbon-14 remaining in the sample as it decays over time.
rubric.description: Explains how carbon dating estimates age
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the remaining amount of carbon-14 (or its decay) is measured to estimate the age of a fossil or other ancient organic material.

modelAnswer: Carbon dating is a method used to determine the age of fossils and other ancient organic materials.
It estimates age by measuring the amount of radioactive carbon-14 remaining in the sample, which decreases as carbon-14 decays.
